name: Quest Requests
description: How every request made in Quest is taken in: chat messages, queued tasks, input sent while work runs and attachments.
purpose: Take every request made in Quest in once, through the same AI, and report its outcome to the person.
approach: Claim each queued task once and honour its schedule and team, accept input while work runs, describe attachments so they can ground the reply, and report the outcome as a decision-request or a note.
out_of_scope: Which representative handles a request (Quest Representatives); how it is planned (Planner).
milestones: 1. Task claims, scheduled-not-due, team scoping and the same request on two surfaces pass on cases.
measures_of_success: Scripted queues show each task claimed once, run when due, reported as an outcome, scoped to its team, and the same request answered alike on two surfaces.
parameters: The queue, the schedule and the team.
inputs: A chat message, a queued task, input sent mid-run or an attachment.
outputs: The request taken in once and its outcome reported.
effects: Claims on tasks; messages and notes to the person.
usage_notes: Run by the lane entry point of the host.

name: Quest Representatives
description: Each request is in the hands of the representative that fits it.
purpose: Put each request in the hands of the representative that fits it.
approach: Choose by assignment, role, thread and the quests each representative holds, keep a thread's representative for the work it spawns, and ask the person only when two fit equally.
out_of_scope: What the representative does with the request; the hub's The Representatives owns the general seat.
milestones: 1. Assigned representatives, threads, reassignment and new-goal owners pass on labelled cases.
measures_of_success: On labelled requests the chosen representative matches the label, work spawned from a thread keeps its representative, and the person is asked only when two fit equally.
parameters: The roles, assignments and visibility of each representative.
inputs: A message, a queued task, a new goal or an autopilot pass, with the quest.
effects: None beyond recording who holds the work.
usage_notes: Reached by the host before the request is planned.

name: Quest Decision Requests
description: A decision reaches the person it belongs to.
purpose: Make a decision reach the person it belongs to.
approach: Put the ask to the assignee on the quest, fall back to a teammate with the right role, hold it on the quest until answered, and never open a duplicate.
out_of_scope: Whether and how to ask in general (the hub's Judgment Calls); acting once the person answers.
milestones: 1. Assignee fallback, team and duplicate-ask cases pass on cases from Quest.
measures_of_success: Scripted quests show an ask reaching the assignee or the fallback teammate, held on the quest until answered, with no duplicate open ask.
parameters: The fallback order and who may decide.
inputs: A step that needs a person and the quest it belongs to.
outputs: A decision-request on the quest, and its answer when it comes.
effects: A record on the quest and a notice to the person.
usage_notes: Reached from the flow when a step is the person's to decide.

name: Intent Evolution
description: Each Quest user discovers what works for their intents.
purpose: Help each Quest user discover what works for their intents.
approach: Read the person's quests and metrics, propose the most likely option with a checkable metric or an experiment when the best is unknown, and keep a goal moving without nagging.
out_of_scope: Placing a message on a quest (Quest Intents); changing the quest (Quest Change Executor); writing the metric (Metric Translation).
milestones: 1. The interface and one first arm exist and are scored on Quest cases with a free rated stage first.
knowledge: The hub has nothing for the second loop of Quest's vision, the user's own intents moving. Quest has an Experiments feature built for finding what works. A pointer to the goal in every reply nags, so restraint is part of the job.
measures_of_success: One balanced number over Quest quests with experiments and outcomes: the reply proposes the most likely option with a checkable metric, or an experiment when the best is unknown, without nagging.
parameters: How often a goal may be nudged, and the metric a quest is judged by.
inputs: A quest with its intents, metrics, history and experiments.
outputs: A proposal: the most likely option with its metric, or an experiment, or nothing when restraint is right.
effects: None until the person accepts a proposal, which is then made through the Quest Change Executor.
usage_notes: Called from the flow in the_self/respond.py and from Quest Autopilot.

name: Hand Off A Goal
description: A new goal lands with the one who can carry it.
purpose: Gives a person the verdicts on who a new goal belongs to and whether an AI representative can take it over at a cost and delay that its metric accepts.
approach: A prompt declared as a prompt spec makes one model call to decide who a new goal belongs to and whether an AI can take it over.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier (choose-a-model-tier) and the surrounding turn or run.
milestones: 1. Its metric has a case set and a recorded result for the current arm and the no-model floor. 2. The model call stays only while it beats the floor on the metric.
knowledge: Proposed 2026-10-28 so that this prompt has a solution and a metric that justify its cost, time and value; not built, so the metric is unmeasured and the current call is a direction, not a measured win.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from the cases without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: The model tier and any cap the module states.
inputs: The text or events the call is given.
outputs: The text or verdict the call returns.
effects: One model call; no write beyond the text it returns.
usage_notes: Selected today: model_judge. The floor is a proposed arm with no model call. Decision teamdec_f95b130faacd (cases relabelled).

name: Guide By Feedback
description: A mistake a person corrected once is not repeated.
purpose: Help the assistant stop repeating a mistake a person has already corrected, so they only have to say it once.
approach: Turn each correction into guidance kept apart from one-off requests and shown where it bears on the turn.
out_of_scope: One-off requests, which are not promoted to permanent rules.
milestones: 1. After a standing correction is stored, the next relevant turn shows it, and no correction that does not bear on the turn is shown, across the feedback sequences.
knowledge: Remembering everything gives perfect recall but turns one-time requests into permanent rules and crowds every prompt, so a ledger separating standing from one-off corrections is needed. The current weakness is precision: with no relevance cut below the card limit, an unrelated rule is shown while room remains. Guidance enters the system prompt as behaviour to follow, not optional context.
measures_of_success: After a standing correction is stored, the next relevant turn shows it, corrections that do not bear on the turn are not shown, and one-off requests are not promoted.
parameters: Cards directory, optional dynamic guidance loader, vector store, provider and model for relevance filtering, a card manager factory, and the number of cards selected per turn.
inputs: A user message and caller scope metadata for selection; correction text, author, location and run dispositions for the ledger.
outputs: A list of guidance cards with bodies for the applicable-guidance block; a catalog and single card reads on demand.
effects: The ledger records observations and writes guidance cards on standing corrections; selection itself is read-only; never raises.
usage_notes: Wire the provider into the orchestrator so selection runs once before planning; rank by relevance when the card limit has room, add a vector or model filter where precision matters.
